newsitem.title: UK: BritGas warns big gas users of supply breaks.
newsitem.headline: BritGas warns big gas users of supply breaks.

text.p: The U.K.'s large gas consumers with interruptible contracts must be prepared for supply disruptions if the weather turns colder this winter, TransCo said on Wednesday.
Failure to turn off the taps when requested could threaten gas supplies to domestic customers, said Andy McPhee, a grid operations manager at TransCo, the pipeline arm of British Gas Plc.
"Customers with interruptible contracts must be prepared to have their supply interrupted during periods of very cold weather," TransCo said in a statement.
"Last winter's severe weather and the consequent huge demand for gas demonstrated that some gas consumers did not understand the basis on which interruptible contracts operate."

Interruptible contracts are a tool used by TransCo to deal with peak winter demand. Gas shippers are offered a discount of 30-40 percent on transportation rates to account for the threat of supply disruption.

Shippers through the TransCo network are given five hours notice before a supply interruption takes place. In turn, shippers are responsible for warning their own interruptible customers -- large commercial gas users --who are expected to be able to switch to alternative fuels or use other contingency arrangements.
If interruptible customers do not cut supplies during periods of peak demand, the system can become overloaded and pressure can fall to dangerously low levels, said McPhee.
"It is vital that when interruption is called then users interrupt supplies and stop using gas," he said. "Failure to do so could result in loss of supply to the domestic load."
An exceptionally cold snap in Scotland last winter resulted in a decision to interrupt all Scottish sites on December 28. But the consumption among interruptible users fell by only 60 percent.
"The response was cause for serious concern," said McPhee. "Supplies to the whole of Glasgow were very much on the margins."

In the event, 4,143 supply points in the Prestonlinks area, to the east of Glasgow, were switched off as the result of interruptible contract holders failing to turn off their own supplies. It took five days for the householders to be fully reconnected, McPhee said.
This winter, gas consumers with interruptible contracts, which include hospitals and prisons, must be prepared to deal with supply disruption, TransCo said.
"TransCo has carried out an extensive communications exercise with shippers and major energy users," the company said in a statement.
"This is to remind them that, in exchange for the cheaper gas delivery under interruptible contracts, commercial gas consumers can be interrupted by TransCo for up to 45 days a year."
